What is the equation of the ellipse given above?
feedback.worked_solution:
Remember that the equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the horizontal radius has length $a=3$ and the vertical radius has length $b=1.5.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{1.5}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{(\frac{{3}^{2}}{{2}^{2}})} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{(\frac{9}{4})} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+\frac{4{y}^{2}}{9} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
